outcome: Presence of premonitory symptoms before or during headache
Types of premonitory symptoms (fatigue, mood change, neck stiffness)
cohort: The study included 100 children and adolescents (18 months to 15 years at headache onset) with migraine who had at least one premonitory symptom recorded at their initial consultation at a Specialist Headache Service in Great Ormond Street Hospital between 1999 and 2015.
finding: Premonitory symptoms, most commonly fatigue, mood change, and neck stiffness, are reported in children with migraine as young as 18 months, presenting a clinical phenotype comparable to adults.
mod_finding: Mode of delivery was recorded, but no findings related to it were reported in the abstract.
gest_age: Gestation at birth was recorded, but no specific range for the cohort was mentioned in the abstract.
